entities.name: Iron-deficiency anemia
observations: In an older man, confirmed iron-deficiency anemia without overt bleeding warrants gastrointestinal evaluation for occult bleeding or malignancy.
Iron replacement should be started while the cause is investigated.

entities.name: Colonoscopy
observations: Colonoscopy is an appropriate component of initial gastrointestinal evaluation for iron-deficiency anemia in an older man, including assessment for colorectal malignancy and other lesions.

entities.name: Bidirectional endoscopy
observations: Preferred initial gastrointestinal investigation for older men with iron-deficiency anemia; combines colonoscopy and EGD, ideally in the same evaluation.

entities.name: Iron replacement
observations: Iron replacement is indicated for documented deficiency; oral iron is generally used if tolerated, while IV iron is reserved for intolerance, ineffective oral therapy, or need for rapid repletion.

entities.name: Capsule endoscopy
observations: Small-bowel capsule evaluation is generally reserved for persistent or recurrent anemia, or inadequate response to iron, after unrevealing high-quality bidirectional endoscopy.
